project_info.application_name: AWS Connected Vehicle Solution - Vehicle Registration Platform
security_objectives: Protect user authentication credentials via Amazon Cognito
Ensure data confidentiality of vehicle registration documents and status
Ensure data integrity of vehicle registration records
Ensure availability of vehicle registration and listing services
Protect data in transit using TLS/HTTPS between all components
Protect data at rest using S3 server-side encryption and DynamoDB encryption
Implement least-privilege IAM permissions for Lambda execution roles
Validate all API inputs to prevent injection and parameter manipulation
Implement API request throttling to prevent abuse
Use detective controls (CloudWatch, AWS Config) for security monitoring
Protect sensitive data in logs (CloudWatch Logs)
Prevent unauthorized deployment of Lambda functions using existing execution roles
Protect against credential stuffing/password spraying on Cognito
Ensure non-repudiation of vehicle registration actions for billing integrity
Protect against domain spoofing and phishing attacks
Perform vulnerability management across all components
Monitor costs proactively to detect anomalous usage patterns
data_assets: Vehicle registration documents (PDF files stored in S3)
Vehicle registration status and metadata (stored in DynamoDB)
User authentication credentials and tokens (managed by Cognito)
API request tokens and session data
GUIDs (globally unique identifiers for API responses)
Pre-signed S3 URLs (temporary access to registration PDFs)
Lambda function execution logs (may contain sensitive data)
Billing and financial records related to vehicle registration
IoT vehicle telemetry data (broader system context)
Diagnostic error codes from connected vehicles (broader system context)
entry_points: REST API endpoints via Amazon API Gateway (ListVehicles, RegisterVehicle, DeregisterVehicle, DescribeVehicle)
AWS Amplify-hosted web front-end (HTML/CSS/JS served to browser)
Amazon Cognito authentication endpoint (user login with challenge/response)
Pre-signed S3 URLs for direct PDF upload/download (browser to S3 bucket)
AWS Management Console (internal actor access to AWS account)
IAM Principal access to DynamoDB tables and S3 buckets
trust_boundaries: Between user browser and AWS Amplify front-end (TLS protected)
Between user browser and Amazon Cognito (authentication challenge/token exchange)
Between user browser and API Gateway (tokens, API methods, data, objects over HTTPS)
Between user browser and S3 bucket (pre-signed URL for direct PDF upload/download)
Between API Gateway and Lambda function (same trust zone - Lambda trusts API Gateway authentication)
Between Lambda function and DynamoDB (GUIDs, data storage/retrieval)
Between Lambda function and S3 bucket (GUIDs, objects storage/retrieval)
Between internal AWS account users and AWS resources (IAM-controlled access)
Between the Connected Vehicle Solution boundary and external users
Between the Vehicle Registration subsystem and the broader Connected Vehicle platform
project_info.summary: The AWS Connected Vehicle Solution is a serverless fleet management platform deployed on AWS, focused on a Vehicle Registration feature that allows fleet managers to register, deregister, list, and describe IoT-connected vehicles. The architecture uses AWS Amplify for the web front-end, Amazon Cognito for authentication/authorization, Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda for REST API processing, Amazon DynamoDB for structured data storage, and Amazon S3 (with server-side encryption) for vehicle registration PDF documents. The system operates within a single AWS account and region, with all services in the same trust zone. Key security concerns identified in the threat model include: (1) credential stuffing/password spraying against Cognito (no MFA), (2) API parameter manipulation for unauthorized resource access, (3) unauthorized Lambda deployment using existing execution roles, (4) data exposure through Lambda function logs, (5) domain spoofing/phishing attacks, (6) data deletion by compromised IAM principals, (7) insufficient authorization controls (single scope for all APIs, all users can perform all operations), and (8) non-repudiation issues for billing disputes. The threat model identifies 11 specific threats across confidentiality, integrity, and availability goals, with 23 proposed mitigations including WAF/Shield protection, input validation, API throttling, encryption at rest, TLS for data in transit, IAM best practices, and detective controls via CloudWatch and AWS Config. Notable assumptions include that MFA is not used, all users can perform all operations (no fine-grained authorization), and the Lambda function trusts all API Gateway requests as pre-authenticated.
project_info.short_summary: AWS serverless vehicle fleet registration platform (Lambda, API Gateway, Cognito, DynamoDB, S3) with 11 identified threats targeting confidentiality, integrity & availability across REST APIs.

all_threats.statement: A remote attacker with knowledge of the Cognito user pool endpoint, can perform credential stuffing or password spraying attacks against the Amazon Cognito authentication endpoint (which lacks MFA), which leads to unauthorized account takeover of fleet manager accounts, resulting in reduced confidentiality of vehicle registration documents, vehicle metadata, and pre-signed S3 URLs.
all_threats.prerequisites: knowledge of the Cognito user pool endpoint and access to breached credential lists
all_threats.threatAction: perform credential stuffing or password spraying attacks against the Amazon Cognito authentication endpoint lacking MFA
all_threats.threatImpact: unauthorized account takeover granting full access to all vehicle registration operations
all_threats.impactedAssets: user authentication credentials and tokens, vehicle registration documents, vehicle registration metadata in DynamoDB

all_threats.statement: An authenticated malicious user with valid Cognito tokens and knowledge of API structure, can manipulate API parameters such as vehicle GUIDs in DescribeVehicle or DeregisterVehicle requests to access or modify other users' resources (IDOR), which leads to unauthorized access to or deletion of vehicle registration records belonging to other fleet managers, resulting in reduced confidentiality and integrity of vehicle registration status and metadata in DynamoDB and registration documents in S3.
all_threats.prerequisites: valid Cognito authentication token and knowledge of or ability to enumerate vehicle GUIDs
all_threats.threatAction: manipulate API parameters (vehicle GUIDs) in REST API calls to access or modify resources belonging to other users due to single-scope authorization for all APIs
all_threats.threatImpact: unauthorized viewing, modification, or deletion of other users' vehicle registration records
all_threats.impactedAssets: vehicle registration documents in S3, vehicle registration status and metadata in DynamoDB, vehicle listing information in DynamoDB

all_threats.statement: A compromised or malicious IAM principal with write/delete permissions on DynamoDB tables and S3 buckets, can delete or corrupt vehicle registration records and PDF documents, which leads to permanent loss of vehicle registration data and inability to prove registration status, resulting in reduced integrity and availability of vehicle registration documents in S3 and vehicle registration metadata in DynamoDB.
all_threats.prerequisites: IAM credentials with write or delete permissions on DynamoDB tables and S3 buckets within the same AWS account
all_threats.threatAction: delete or corrupt vehicle registration records in DynamoDB and PDF documents in S3
all_threats.threatImpact: permanent loss or corruption of vehicle registration data affecting fleet operations and billing integrity
all_threats.impactedAssets: vehicle registration documents in S3, vehicle registration status and metadata in DynamoDB, billing and financial records related to vehicle registration

all_threats.statement: An internal developer or compromised CI/CD pipeline with IAM permissions to create Lambda functions, can deploy a malicious Lambda function using an existing overly-permissive execution role, which leads to unauthorized access to DynamoDB data, S3 objects, and other AWS resources accessible by that role, resulting in reduced confidentiality of vehicle registration documents, vehicle metadata, and user data.
all_threats.threatSource: internal developer or compromised CI/CD pipeline
all_threats.prerequisites: IAM permissions to create or update Lambda functions and knowledge of existing Lambda execution role ARNs
all_threats.threatAction: deploy a malicious Lambda function that assumes an existing execution role with broad permissions to exfiltrate data from DynamoDB and S3
all_threats.threatImpact: unauthorized access to all data accessible by the Lambda execution role including vehicle records and registration documents
all_threats.impactedAssets: vehicle registration documents in S3, vehicle registration status and metadata in DynamoDB, Lambda function execution logs

all_threats.statement: A remote attacker with the ability to intercept or guess pre-signed S3 URLs, can access vehicle registration PDF documents directly from S3 without authenticating through the API Gateway, which leads to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive vehicle registration documents, resulting in reduced confidentiality of vehicle registration documents stored in S3.
all_threats.prerequisites: ability to intercept network traffic, access browser history, or predict pre-signed URL parameters before expiration
all_threats.threatAction: access pre-signed S3 URLs to download vehicle registration PDF documents without proper authentication
all_threats.threatImpact: unauthorized disclosure of sensitive vehicle registration documents
all_threats.impactedAssets: vehicle registration documents (PDF files stored in S3)

all_threats.statement: A malicious actor with the ability to craft phishing emails or create spoofed domains, can impersonate the vehicle registration platform to trick fleet managers into submitting credentials on a fake login page, which leads to credential theft and subsequent unauthorized access to the legitimate platform, resulting in reduced confidentiality of user authentication credentials and vehicle registration data.
all_threats.prerequisites: ability to register similar domain names and craft convincing phishing emails targeting fleet managers
all_threats.threatAction: create a spoofed domain mimicking the AWS Amplify-hosted web front-end to harvest Cognito credentials from fleet managers
all_threats.threatImpact: credential theft enabling unauthorized access to vehicle registration operations and data
all_threats.impactedAssets: user authentication credentials and tokens, vehicle registration documents, vehicle registration status and metadata

all_threats.statement: A remote attacker with network access to the API Gateway endpoints, can send crafted injection payloads (NoSQL injection, command injection) through API input parameters such as vehicle identifiers or registration fields, which leads to unauthorized data retrieval or manipulation in DynamoDB or unintended Lambda code execution, resulting in reduced integrity of vehicle registration status and metadata in DynamoDB.
all_threats.prerequisites: network access to API Gateway REST endpoints and knowledge of API parameter structure
all_threats.threatAction: send crafted injection payloads through RegisterVehicle or DescribeVehicle API parameters targeting DynamoDB queries in Lambda functions
all_threats.threatImpact: unauthorized data retrieval, modification, or unintended code execution within Lambda functions
all_threats.impactedAssets: vehicle registration status and metadata in DynamoDB, Lambda function execution environment

all_threats.statement: An operations engineer or automated log analysis tool with access to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, can view sensitive data inadvertently logged by Lambda functions during execution (e.g., registration details, authentication tokens, PII), which leads to exposure of sensitive vehicle and user information through log data, resulting in reduced confidentiality of vehicle registration documents, user data, and API request tokens.
all_threats.threatSource: operations engineer or automated log analysis tool
all_threats.prerequisites: read access to Amazon CloudWatch Logs containing Lambda function execution output
all_threats.threatAction: view or extract sensitive data (PII, registration details, tokens) inadvertently written to CloudWatch Logs by Lambda functions
all_threats.threatImpact: exposure of sensitive vehicle registration data and authentication tokens through log files
all_threats.impactedAssets: Lambda function execution logs, vehicle registration status and metadata, API request tokens and session data

all_threats.statement: A remote attacker with network access, can flood the API Gateway endpoints with high volumes of requests (DDoS or application-layer abuse), which leads to API throttling exhaustion, elevated Lambda concurrency costs, and degraded service availability, resulting in reduced availability of vehicle registration and listing services and increased operational costs.
all_threats.prerequisites: network access to API Gateway endpoints (potentially with valid or stolen authentication tokens)
all_threats.threatAction: flood API Gateway endpoints with high volumes of ListVehicles, RegisterVehicle, or DescribeVehicle requests to exhaust throttling limits and drive up Lambda invocations
all_threats.threatImpact: service degradation or unavailability for legitimate fleet managers and anomalous cost increases
all_threats.impactedAssets: REST API endpoints via Amazon API Gateway, Lambda function compute resources, vehicle registration and listing services

all_threats.statement: An authenticated user involved in a billing dispute with no fine-grained audit trail, can deny having performed a vehicle registration or deregistration action, which leads to inability to prove which user initiated a specific registration operation, resulting in reduced integrity of billing and financial records related to vehicle registration (non-repudiation failure).
all_threats.threatSource: authenticated user involved in a billing dispute
all_threats.prerequisites: valid Cognito authentication and absence of fine-grained audit logging tying user identity to specific registration actions
all_threats.threatAction: deny having performed a RegisterVehicle or DeregisterVehicle action to dispute associated billing charges
all_threats.threatImpact: inability to attribute registration actions to specific users for billing and compliance purposes
all_threats.impactedAssets: billing and financial records related to vehicle registration, vehicle registration status and metadata in DynamoDB

all_threats.statement: A low-skilled attacker with access to the public web front-end, can enumerate vehicle GUIDs by observing API response patterns or exploiting predictable identifiers in the ListVehicles endpoint, which leads to discovery of valid vehicle identifiers that can be used in subsequent IDOR attacks, resulting in reduced confidentiality of vehicle listing information stored in DynamoDB.
all_threats.prerequisites: access to the AWS Amplify-hosted web front-end and a valid Cognito authentication token
all_threats.threatAction: enumerate vehicle GUIDs by analyzing API responses from the ListVehicles endpoint to build a catalog of valid vehicle identifiers
all_threats.threatImpact: discovery of valid vehicle GUIDs enabling targeted unauthorized access attempts via other API endpoints
all_threats.impactedAssets: GUIDs (globally unique identifiers), vehicle listing information in DynamoDB

all_threats.statement: A malicious actor with access to a misconfigured or publicly exposed S3 bucket policy, can directly access vehicle registration PDF documents bypassing API Gateway and Cognito authentication entirely, which leads to bulk unauthorized disclosure of sensitive registration documents, resulting in reduced confidentiality of vehicle registration documents stored in S3.
all_threats.prerequisites: discovery of the S3 bucket name and existence of an overly permissive bucket policy or ACL misconfiguration
all_threats.threatAction: directly access or list objects in the S3 bucket containing vehicle registration PDFs without going through the application's authentication layer
all_threats.threatImpact: bulk unauthorized disclosure of vehicle registration PDF documents
all_threats.impactedAssets: vehicle registration documents (PDF files stored in S3)

## Attack Tree Summary

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Threat ID** | T001 |
| **Root Goal** | Unauthorized account takeover → exfiltration of vehicle registration data |
| **Attack Path 1** | **Credential Stuffing** — Attacker enumerates valid accounts, cross-references breached credential databases, and replays stolen username/password pairs against the MFA-less Cognito endpoint |
| **Attack Path 2** | **Password Spraying** — Attacker harvests fleet manager usernames via OSINT, then systematically sprays common passwords at low velocity to avoid account lockout detection |
| **Convergence Point** | Both paths yield valid Cognito JWT tokens, enabling authenticated API Gateway access |
| **Terminal Impact** | Exfiltration of vehicle registration documents (S3), vehicle metadata (DynamoDB), and authentication tokens for persistent unauthorized access |
| **Key Enablers** | Absence of MFA on Cognito, publicly reachable authentication endpoint, lack of aggressive rate limiting, and password reuse by fleet managers |
